reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation of spatial perception hinges on the coordination of sensory surfaces—visual for sighted individuals and tactile for the blind. Each sensory input initiates a directional feeling (D), which must be prolonged into space through a common object (O) formed between skin and external space. This process necessitates that the skin and space beyond coalesce into a unified object for another sensory surface, such as the eye or other skin regions. For the blind, this linkage occurs via motion-coupled skin regions, forming an extrusion of space. As tactile exploration proceeds, it constructs a felt spatial sphere (R) around the body, expanding with locomotion. The system's failure mode arises when sensory surfaces cannot form a coherent object, breaking the continuity of spatial perception. The resulting structure supports both Bayesian inference in GSI and dynamic state transitions in GSE.
